prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1118; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's policyholder after a rear-end collision at a signalled intersection. Claimant is represented by counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office. Initial injury report notes a concussion.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle and that the accident occurred as described. The other driver's account matches in every key detail.

Entry 4: Photographs of the rear bumper and tail lamp assembly show damage that is mostly consistent with the reported impact speed. A few old scratches on the left quarter panel may predate this crash and are noted for separate review.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant through counsel. The account of the collision was the same as in the first call and in the written statement, with no changes to sequence or position of vehicles.

Entry 6: Medical records show the claimant's treatment followed a usual course for a concussion and eased off as symptoms improved. No prior injury to the head or neck area is known from the records requested so far.

Entry 7: It is not yet clear whether the current symptoms are caused by this crash. Requested an independent medical review and prior records from the claimant's primary care provider to clarify the link.

Entry 8: File is on hold pending the medical review and the response to the records request. Next review is scheduled once those documents arrive, with counsel copied on the status update.
